Subject: Questions on MSA indemnity (defense control + evidence)

Connor —

Thanks for sending the MSA redline yesterday (attached as nf_msa_redline_v2.docx). Our legal team has two quick, practical questions before we proceed to procurement: 

1) Defense / control: the current clause v3 says vendor will "assume defense" for third-party IP claims but reserves the right to appoint counsel. We need clarity on whether NovaForge must consent to counsel selection and what approval rights we have for settlement that affects our products.

2) Evidence & logs: If we receive a notice of infringement tied to model output, who on the vendor side will be responsible for collecting the technical evidence (logs, prompt history, model version, embeddings snapshot)? We need an operational owner and a retention timeframe.

We can live with standard legal positions if there's a clear operational handoff (who collects what, how long you keep it, and how you deliver it to us). Procurement is on standby but wants these answers before signing.

Attached: nf_msa_redline_v2.docx (redlines)

Thanks Beth — great, clear asks. Looping in Kimberly and Priyom from Legal and Ben (your AM) to propose an operational handoff. High level answers:

- Defense/control: Redwood accepts defense for third-party IP claims that stem from our hosted model output; we typically reserve the right to select counsel but we do not settle any claim that would materially impair the customer's product or rights without consent. Kimberly / Priyom: will propose concrete language below.

Suggested retention: 18 months, with a secure export process to deliver to the customer upon notice. Priyom / Kimberly: please confirm whether 18 months is acceptable from a legal perspective.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: RE: Questions on MSA indemnity (defense control + evidence)

Beth / Connor —

Thanks for the clear framing. Below are the legal positions we'd propose to put into the MSA redline. These are intended to be operationally implementable and avoid open-ended exposure for either party.

1) Defense / Control (proposed snippet):
"""
Vendor shall have the right to assume and control the defense and settlement of any third-party claim alleging that Customer's authorized use of the Services infringes a third party's intellectual property rights; provided that Vendor shall not, without Customer's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld), enter into any settlement that (a) admits fault by Customer, (b) imposes an obligation or financial liability on Customer, or (c) requires Customer to cease use of the Services.
"""

This preserves vendor-led defense while protecting NovaForge from unilateral settlements. If NovaForge prefers counsel selection rights, we can agree to a right of approval for counsel with a short list process but that can slow response time.

2) Evidence collection & retention (proposed snippet):
"""
Upon receipt of a claim notice, Vendor shall preserve and, where reasonably requested by Customer, provide evidence reasonably related to the alleged claim, including but not limited to service logs, prompt and metadata snapshots, model version identifiers, and embeddings or other relevant artifacts. Vendor shall retain such evidence for a period of 18 months from the date of creation unless otherwise agreed. Vendor will provide a secure, encrypted export of the preserved evidence to Customer within a commercially reasonable timeframe following request.
"""

Operational notes: Priyom / Connor, confirming that Redwood's evidence export will be encrypted and contain a signed manifest; also confirm SLA for export (we suggest 10 business days from confirmed request). Beth — if your e-discovery or litigation team needs a different timeframe, flag now.

Open items:
- Retention: customer requested 24 months in the past. We propose 18 months as a compromise given storage/cost and typical claim windows.
- Export SLA: propose 10 business days; can be tightened for Enterprise with fee/commitments.
- Evidence scope: we intentionally excluded raw model weights and training datasets; this is about runtime artifacts.

Happy to take comments; we can convert these snippets into redline language if you confirm the general approach.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear language and the walk-through. A few follow ups from NovaForge: 

1) Retention: our preference is 24 months because our internal claim window and regulatory obligations in some lines of business run longer. Would Redwood accept 24 months for hosted evidence? If not, please explain the specific cost / operational constraints so we can evaluate. 

2) Logs & scope: the snippet is helpful but we need to be explicit about what is considered "service logs" — specifically, we need at minimum (a) full prompt (including system and user messages), (b) the model identifier and quantization level, (c) timestamped token output, and (d) request headers including customer tenant id. If Redwood can't provide full tokenized output for privacy reasons, we need an agreed-upon redaction pattern.

3) Export chain-of-custody: procurement wants an assurance the export will be hashed and time-stamped (or a signed manifest) for admissibility. Your note about signed manifest is good; please add concrete wording to the export procedure.

Procurement (copied) — if NovaForge can get 18 months plus an option to extend to 24 months for an enterprise commitment, are you comfortable moving forward?

We can do a 30-min sync if that helps.

Thanks,
Beth
Beth Stone
Sr. Counsel, NovaForge

Subject: Final: operational handoff & next steps re: indemnity redlines

Beth / team —

Thanks for the constructive back-and-forth and procurement's willingness to be flexible. Summary and proposed next steps so procurement/legal can sign off: 

1) Retention: Redwood confirms 18 months standard retention for runtime evidence. We will offer an upgrade path to 24 months as an Order Form option for Enterprise customers (we can reflect this as an optional line item in the Order Form). NovaForge procurement: if you elect the 24-month option, we'll include it in the final SO and adjust pricing accordingly.

2) Evidence scope: Redwood will preserve the following artifacts on notice: full system+user prompt text, model identifier and version (including quantization flag), timestamped token output (where legal/contractually permissible), request headers including tenant id, and sampled runtime metadata (sampling seed, top-k/top-p). If full token output cannot be exported due to tenant privacy constraints, we will provide a redacted token stream along with a signed statement describing the redaction method.

3) Export & chain-of-custody: Priyom will produce an export manifest hashed and signed by Redwood's HSM, and deliver evidence via an encrypted HTTPS transfer to NovaForge's designated secure bucket. SLA for encrypted export: 10 business days from confirmation of valid legal request.

Owners / operational contacts: 
- Evidence collection & export lead: Priyom Das (priyom_das@redwoodinference.com) — will coordinate the manifest and run the export.
- Order Form / pricing: Lauren Bishop (lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com) — will prepare the optional 24-month line item and pricing impact.
- Sales/coordination: Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwoodinference.com)

Kimberly / Priyom: please convert the agreed snippets into the final redline for the MSA and confirm the wording for the Order Form option. Beth: if NovaForge can accept the 18-month standard + optional 24-month paid upgrade, Procurement indicated that should be sufficient to move to signature.

I'll follow up with a short runbook and link to the shared folder with the redline once Kimberly posts it.
